items.title: A24’s Elden Ring Movie Costs Nearly $200 Million
items.summary: A24’s Elden Ring adaptation is reportedly its most expensive film to date, with a nearly $200 million budget and a planned 2028 release.
items.content:
A24’s Elden Ring adaptation is reportedly its most expensive film to date, with a nearly $200 million budget and a planned 2028 release. A24’s previous most expensive release was Marty Supreme, with a budget of around $70 million, which surpassed the previous leader, Civil War, with a budget of about $50 million.

The relatively new FromSoftware franchise is seeing a quick turnaround in its screen adaptation. The game launched in February 2022 and features world-building courtesy of George R. R. Martin. To date, the game has sold over 36 million copies across Steam, PlayStation, and XBOX, and it’s known for its challenging gameplay.

The movie has a March 3, 2028 release date, and a new Wall Street Journal report says it will cost around $200 million to make. The report highlighted how A24 has become a major player in the film industry, with many now trying to copy its formula.

Major studios, meanwhile, are increasingly trying to copy the A24 playbook. Online horror properties that seem like they could become the next “Backrooms” have sparked multimillion-dollar bidding wars. Universal is backing a big-budget movie from the “Everything Everywhere” directors. “They’re a Goldilocks company. Just the right amount of people doing just the right amount of things,” said Julie Huntsinger, the Telluride director.

According to The Hollywood Reporter , Alex Garland will write and direct the movie, the same person who wrote and directed Civil War. The cast includes Kit Connor, Tom Burke, Rose Liu, and Nick Offerman , among others. The film is also expected to take about 100 days of principal photography.

Gaming franchises are a major trend right now, and Nick Offerman has also signed on for the upcoming 4th Sonic the Hedgehog film. Learn more about that here .

What are your thoughts on the upcoming Eldon Ring film? Sound off about this story and all others in our official Discord server.

For more Insider gaming coverage, check out the latest on Michael B. Jordan’s Battlefield film. Also, don’t forget to sign up for our weekly newsletter .

I'm Robert DeFelice. I spent years covering pro-wrestling industry for outlets such as Fightful. After years in wrestling journalism, I’ve transitioned to video games, another passion of mine.

items.title: PC users get dose of PS1 nostalgia with free Elden Ring meets Resident Evil taster
items.content:
Gamers nostalgic for something that resembles the early PlayStation days should look no further than False Oath.

Resident Evil fans are going to love this new PC exclusive, as it’s exactly what we’d imagine a game like Elden Ring would look like had it launched for the OG PlayStation.

As a console player, I’m horrendously jealous of the PC users, now more than ever after seeing the rumoured price for Xbox Project Helix .

Video game graphics are constantly improving and as such, the price of hardware is skyrocketing. Part of me wishes I’d just caved and bought a PC back in the day.

I’m even more jealous of PC users though after trying the False Oath demo on my Steam Deck.

Developed by Daniel Almenara and Nytelynn, False Oath is an upcoming Steam game that pays homage to PS1 games like Resident Evil , Dino Crisis, and more.

The synopsis reads: “ False Oath is a retro-style survival horror game set in a medieval era. A deadly plague spreads across the kingdom. Search for a cure before it’s too late.”

After looking at the screenshots and gameplay footage, you can tell the FromSoftware vibes are strong with this one. It’s very Kings Field -esque, but it’s exactly the type of game I’d picture in my head if you told me to imagine the likes of Elden Ring , Dark Souls or Demon Souls as a PS1 game.

It’s got a retro eeriness I haven’t seen since Crow Country , and it stands out from other games in the genre. I’m honestly surprised the idea hasn’t been done sooner.

False Oath is due to launch in Q1 of 2027 exclusively for PCs, but in the meantime, you can play a free demo to get a taste of what’s to come.

Despite Steam yielding no answer on whether the demo would work on Steam Deck, I threw caution to the wind and gave it a go anyway.

It didn’t work flawlessly, but it did the trick for some first impressions of the story, world design, and general gameplay. Hopefully when the full-game releases, it’ll be optimised for the Steam Deck.

From my own experience, I’d confidently say this is a game for me, and again that’s speaking as a huge fan of both Resident Evil and FromSoftware games. This scratches my itch for more modernised retro throwbacks .

It has that authentic clunkiness you’d expect from a game like this, and if the visuals weren’t so crisp, I’d have been fully convinced that this was some sort of long-lost PS1 game.

items.title: Elden Ring: Only 23.9% Finish It vs 36% Median [2026]
items.summary: Only 23.9% of players finish Elden Ring, far below the 36% median. See where players quit, how it compares, and what the 2026 data shows.
items.content:
Elden Ring players are finishing the game at rates that look high at first glance, but the hard numbers tell a more mixed story. Steam’s global achievement statistics list 23.9% of owners with the Elden Lord achievement and 10.4% with all 42 achievements. Those are the cleanest figures in circulation on October 23, 2026, and they now anchor a viral claim that Elden Ring fans are built different .

Elden Ring Completion Rate: The Verified Numbers What Steam’s Achievement Data Actually Measures The Funnel From Roundtable Hold to Elden Lord Where Players Leave: Reading the Drop-Offs The early game holds its audience The mid-game and late-game cliffs Testing the Built-Different Claim The 19-Game Comparison and Its 36% Median The 40% Figure Nobody Can Source What HowLongToBeat Adds: 60 Hours Versus 136 Fanatical’s 34.89% and 42.13%: Different Labels, Different Games Why Completion Statistics Mislead Market Impact: Why Publishers Care About Finish Rates Historical Context: How Completion Became a Scoreboard Competitive Comparison: Elden Ring Against the Pack Predictions: What Happens Next The Takeaway FAQ What percentage of players have beaten Elden Ring? How many players earn all 42 Elden Ring achievements? Is the Elden Ring completion rate higher than most games? Is it true that 40% of players beat the final boss? Which Elden Ring boss achievement has the lowest completion rate? How long does Elden Ring take to finish? What do Fanatical’s Beat It and Conquered It numbers mean? Are Elden Ring fans really built different? Related Coverage FRVR is among the outlets running the story, which pitches the Elden Ring completion rate as higher than most other games. The data does not fully back that framing. One comparison of 19 single-player games reports an ending-achievement rate of about 24% for Elden Ring against a median of about 36% for the whole set. That puts the game about 12 points below the middle of that pack, not above it.

This analysis sorts out what each figure measures, where the numbers stop and speculation starts, and what the debate says about how the industry reads completion data. For a sense of the audience behind these percentages, our coverage of the Steam hardware and software survey shows how large and varied the Steam player base is.

The week's biggest stories in tech, gaming and security, in one email.

Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.

Before any argument about who is built different, it helps to separate what is confirmed from what is repeated. The fact base for this story is narrow, and every figure below traces to a named source. Where a claim lacks a method, a date, or a platform, this article says so and keeps it out of the main analysis.

Three claims fail the same test. The headline idea that Elden Ring fans are built different has no measurable definition. The statement that roughly 40% of players have beaten the final boss comes with no method, platform, date, or source in the available material. And the broad line that the game’s completion rate beats most other games rests on a single comparison set that does not support it on the ending metric.

Steam’s global achievement page reports the share of all owners who have unlocked each achievement. That denominator matters. It counts everyone who bought the game, including people who never launched it, people who played an hour and drifted away, and people who own it only because it sat in a bundle or a sale. A completion rate built on owners will always read lower than one built on active players.

So when Steam lists 23.9% for Elden Lord, the plain reading is that just under one in four owners has earned that achievement. It does not say that 23.9% of people who seriously tried the game reached that point. The true rate among committed players is higher, but no available source quantifies it. Anyone quoting a higher number without naming the denominator is guessing.

The same logic applies to the 10.4% figure for all 42 achievements. A full-achievement run asks for far more than a story finish, so it works as a ceiling on dedication rather than a measure of ordinary completion. Roughly one owner in ten has cleared every item on the list, which is a meaningful number for a long game with a reputation for punishment, but it is not proof of a unique fan base.

Steam’s per-achievement percentages let us build a rough funnel. The table below orders the confirmed figures from highest to lowest and adds two derived columns. The first shows the points lost against the row above, and the second shows what share of the previous row’s players kept going. Note that the order reflects the percentages, not a guaranteed play sequence, since players can tackle some bosses in a different order.

Source: Steam global achievement statistics for Elden Ring. Derived columns are this site’s arithmetic on the listed percentages.

The first two steps lose very little. Going from Roundtable Hold at 75.0% to Margit, the Fell Omen at 71.0% costs 4 points, and Shardbearer Godrick at 65.1% costs another 5.9. About 94.7% and 91.7% of the previous group carried on. For a game with a hard reputation, that is a sticky opening. One in four owners never reaches Roundtable Hold at all, which may point to a pool of buyers who barely started.

items.title: Nearly 10 million people have played Elden Ring for over 100 hours, analyst says – and close to 3.5 million of them have all the achievements
items.summary: FromSoftware sickos are out in force on this one
items.content:
FromSoftware sickos are out in force on this one

FromSoftware 's landmark action-RPG has sold pretty well since its 2022 release, and a significant portion of those buyers have accrued significant playtime in the fantasy juggernaut.

Rhys Elliott, head of market analytics at Alinea Analytics, posted some numbers on Twitter about what Elden Ring's managed to achieve to date. The topline figures are nothing surprising: FromSoftware's last epic has shifted approximately 36.4 million copies on Steam, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, and it's brought in around $2 billion dollars in total revenue.

Those are the kind of numbers you get when you have people like Post Malone and multi-time WWE Champion Randy Orton openly talking about picking it up and becoming immersed in the struggle. It takes a certain kind of popularity to even grab their attention, and then they become part of the advertising by discussing it so publicly.

Elden Ring has sold 36.4M copies on Steam, PlayStation, and Xbox, generating $2B in revenue (@alineaanalytics estimates). Wildly, over 9.8M people have played Elden Ring for over 100 hours, with nearly 3.5M people getting all of the achievements/trophies. For reference, 10.9% of Elden Ring’s PlayStation players have the platinum trophy, while 10.5% of players on Steam and 3.9% of Xbox players unlocked all the achievements. Git gud, Xbox players! By many accounts, including my own, Elden Ring is one of the best games of all time. It’s an evergreen seller that will continue to be a cash cow for Bandai and FromSoftware for years to come. Elden Ring has sold another 2M copies across Steam, PlayStation, and Xbox this year, generating almost $110M. This means it’s outperforming many of this year’s high-profile releases. Even Elden Ring’s standalone run-based PvE spinoff, 2025’s Nightreign, has sold 7.8M copies and generated $282M in revenue. Hell yeah. More on Substack. October 22, 2026

But the real revelation of Alinea's findings comes afterward. Around 9.8 million of those players have put over 100 hours into roaming the Lands Between. That's a pretty significant chunk of the community.

It's hard to compare these things through hard data, but I would be surprised if this wasn't quite rare across role-playing games. I suspect the portion of the audience for Final Fantasy 7 Remake , any of the Yakuza series, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, or whatever who manage something similar is a smaller minority.

4,000 hours into Elden Ring, streamer commissions a custom mod so he can beat it another 726 times Baldur's Gate 3 has sold over 23m copies, but only 1% of players have crossed 500 hour in playtime Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has sold 8.7 million copies and made $366 million, analyst says What's more, Elliott says almost 3.5 million have gotten every achievement. These people have more patience and gumption than I do, that's for sure. I've never been a trophy hunter in games, and I definitely am not tempted by any of FromSoftware's fare.

If you're included in these portions of Elden Ring, I applaud you and hope you have healthy coping mechanisms for the frustration and intensity they entail. "By many accounts, including my own, Elden Ring is one of the best games of all time," Elliott writes. "It's an evergreen seller that will continue to be a cash cow for Bandai and FromSoftware for years to come."

Considering there's a movie coming in 2028, there's a good chance the fanbase will only get bigger, too. Long live Hidetaka Miyazaki.

items.title: PlayStation Plus free Elden Ring alternative drops huge update with unexpected musical twist
items.content:
Mortal Shell 2 is free to try with PlayStation Plus and the latest update makes it more of a must-play than ever.

One of the best additions to PlayStation Plus in a long time just received a major content update.

Earlier this month PlayStation Plus was bolstered with a superb batch of freebies, with Horizon: Forbidden West and Mafia: The Old Country taking center stage.

It wasn’t just the Extra library that saw some great, new additions though. PlayStation Plus Premium subscribers got a new free trial for an Elden Ring rival like no other; Mortal Shell 2 .

Simply put Mortal Shell 2 redefines what it means to be a souls game, and it’s up there with the likes of Nioh and Lies of P in my humble opinion. It tackles my biggest issue with FromSoftware's work .

After launching in August earlier this year Mortal Shell 2 has dropped a major content update with some excellent improvements/additions.

For starters, a new photomode is going to be a big hit with players wishing to express their artistic side.

Some new cosmetic skins have been added for deeper customisation and they’re joined by 10 new tarstones. These are items used to upgrade your gear, so you’ve got more options for your builds now.

Delving deeper still is 15 new dungeons to explore, and you can enjoy these with Overkill graphics.

The musical twist however comes through a new type of lute. Mortal Shell 2 went viral for letting you use a lute as a weapon and the new Impervious Lute lets you lure enemies in with the sound of your sweet melodies. There are even some additional tracks to play on your shiny, new instrument.

Keeping with the music theme, the game also has an alternative soundtrack now. It was composed by Rotting Christ's Sakis Tolis and will be a fitting change for those who want to make the game a shade darker.

All of this is completely free, and available now. Some very meaningful changes have been made here so we’re excited to jump back in, but if you’re yet to play you can learn more about the game below.

Mortal Shell 2 is a completely different beast to FromSoftware’s soulsborne games. The way it stands out from the crowd is through its ‘shells’.

Rather than putting players in boxes and forcing them to choose a build and stick with it, Mortal Shell 2’s main gimmick is the ability to switch as you go. Each ‘shell’ is a body with its own unique stats, strengths and shortcomings.

items.title: Elden Ring Update 1.26 Pushed Out on October 20
items.summary: Elden Ring update 1.26 is live on October 20 as part of the game's downtime, and this is for a minor patch.
items.content:
FromSoftware has released a minor update for Elden Ring on all platforms this October 20, and it should be live now as part of today’s downtime.

The servers for the Souls-like game have been taken down on October 20, and this is to roll out Elden Ring update 1.26 .

Read on for the known issues and other tidbits of info from today’s patch.

Update : Yep, FromSoftware did fix the arrow exploit among other bugs squashed.

First off, the maintenance period starts at 12:00 am PDT/3 am PDT/4 pm JST/9 am CEST and ends after three hours.

Of course, this could go on longer, but generally, FromSoftware sticks to their downtime schedule.

As for the patch, it should be a minor one, and we have a pretty good idea what’s being fixed. There is a known glitch/exploit spotted fairly recently that messes up PvP encounters in Elden Ring.

This bug allowed, Thanks to Arrow rain paired with Pique arrows, to instantly build up any status after a single hit. As you can see, this could very much mess up PvP fights.

So far, FromSoftware hasn’t released the patch notes, but we wouldn’t be surprised if this is included in the changelog.

Stay tuned to this article, as we’ll update it once the official changelog is live.

items.title: New Elden Ring Mini Replicas Arrive: Malenia, Messmer & Wylder

items.content:
Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

items.title: Elden Ring On Switch 2 – The Worst Way To Play The Best Game
items.summary: Elden Ring on Switch 2 gets the job done admirably, but it is the inferior version of a fantastic game. - Game Informer

items.title: I Tested Elden Ring On Switch 2 In A Cozy Cafe And It Ran Just Fine, Which Is Great News For A Remarkable Game
items.summary: You shouldn't play it in the rain/but you can play it on a train
items.content:
Elden Ring is an excellent, excellent video game. It’s got that smashy FromSoftware combat, a couple hundred boss fights that are all (mostly) unique and fun, character build customization for miles, a gorgeous and massive open world that’s a treat to explore, an intriguing story and hidden secrets, and a robust DLC that could be a game all its own. There’s a reason (well, many reasons!) why it’s almost universally critically acclaimed and still beloved by fans a few years after launch, too.

I love Elden Ring ! But when Ethan asked me to take on the review of the Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2, I wasn’t, like, stoked about it. I beat Elden Ring back when it first came out, easily dumping over 100 hours into the main game and probably another solid 40 or more into the DLC. And I played the Tarnished Edition at a preview event earlier this year for about 20 minutes, after which time I told everyone I spoke with about the experience that yup, that was Elden Ring all right! Elden Ring on a Switch 2! Game’s great, but I don’t necessarily need to play it again. What else is there to say?

It turns out, after playing for review, I do have one additional thing to say: Elden Ring is, apparently, pretty fun to play in public. Ideally at a cozy coffee shop with squoshy chairs where you can purchase hot London fogs to drink while you play.

Elden Ring was technically playable on the go before the Tarnished Edition , for folks with a Steam Deck. I have one of those, but the device, unlike the Switch 2, is not fun to take out in public. It’s heavy to hold, does not have a convenient kickstand, and you have to hold it in your hands to play if you don’t want to drag a controller around too. With the Switch 2, I could set the console on the table with the kickstand out, take the Joy-Cons off, lean back in my chair, and play Elden Ring while soothing cafe music played in the background. Every time I die (which is often), I get a nice sip of tea. I do not rage. I do not tense up. Helpfully, the cat (who is not here in the cafe with me) does not butt her head against the triggers and cause me to swing my sword randomly. Life is good.

In basically every other respect, I stick to my guns from the preview: this is Elden Ring ! It’s on the Switch 2 now! There were concerns after the first round of early previews that it ran poorly, but those were fixed by the time I previewed it earlier this year and remain fixed now. It runs fine. There are still occasional little framerate drops and yeah, it doesn’t look quite as nice as it will on your PS5 or Xbox Series, but who cares? It still plays great. The minor technical compromises didn’t interfere with combat in any way that was meaningful to me. It still looks good. It’s still lovely to stand on a cliff’s edge and look out in the direction of the Erdtree, the sun’s rays glistening through the clouds and a skyline of crumbling ruin all around.

I should mention that the Tarnished Edition does not have any meaningful new features. There are four new armor sets, a bit of customization for Torrent, and two new starting classes. Unfortunately, two of those new armor sets are starting sets for the two new classes, Heavy Knight and Idus Knight. I played as the Idus Knight and replaced my armor almost immediately with some tunic thing I got off a knight in the very first part of Limgrave, because it had better stats. I think I wore this same tunic when I played the game the first time. Shame, because the new starting armor genuinely looked great. I found the addition of these two new classes to be extremely whatever: you’re going to customize all your stats and replace all your gear almost immediately anyway. The Idus Knight was just a Samurai two levels lower, with different equipment. These additions did nothing for me, and certainly will do nothing for anyone after the first hour of game.

This release does include the superb Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, bundled right in from the start, though. That rules.

But who cares? It’s Elden Ring , on Switch 2! I can easily play it on a plane or on a train, in a box or with a fox, here or there, anywhere! I can take it to bars, to rooftop wine parties. I can play it outside on a patio with a cold one in a koozie next to me as the summer sun sets. I recognize that this is just effectively restating the main gimmick of the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2, but I admittedly haven’t taken my Switch 2 out much since it launched last year. Elden Ring , the best game of 2022 and arguably one of the best games of the decade, is a great excuse to do so. Give it a shot. Order yourself a latte or, a little later in the day, maybe a nice glass of pinot noir, bust out your Switch 2, and give it a shot.

This article was corrected post-publication: Limveld is Nightreign , Limgrave is Elden Ring . I can never keep them straight.

items.title: Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching Aug. 28 on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Pre-order available. Explore a breathtaking world full of excitement and mystery.
items.content:
08/11/26 Pre-order now Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching Aug. 28 on Nintendo Switch 2 The Lands Between—a place of myth, gods, and broken dreams. Long ago, Queen Marika and her divine offspring reigned here, but since the Elden Ring was shattered, the world has fallen into decay. Now, the land whispers for a King.

The “Tarnished,” long exiled, are finally seeing the light of Grace once more. Step into this hauntingly beautiful realm, unravel its ancient mysteries, and rise as the one true Elden Lord.

The ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition game arrives on the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system on August 28 .

The Lands Between are part of a vast continent, where magnificent open fields and huge dungeons with complex three-dimensional designs are seamlessly connected. As you explore, the joy of discovering unknown and overwhelming threats awaits you.

Mastery of the terrain and knowledge of its secrets can help you overcome enemies and defeat formidable bosses—or lead invading players into traps.

The founding mythology of Elden Ring was written by George R. R. Martin and adapted into a rich multilayered story. Intersecting goals and desires between the characters create an intense narrative that weaves throughout the Lands Between. The events of the game can unravel in many ways—depending on your interventions.

Combat is simple to learn yet offers hidden depths of dexterity. As you seek to become the Elden Lord, you’ll need to explore the balance between attacking, avoiding damage, using a wide variety of weapons, spells, summons, and perfecting your timing to take advantage of your opponents’ weaknesses.

In addition to customizing the appearance of your character, there are countless ways to combine the weapons, armor, usable items, and magic that you equip. You can develop your character according to your play style.

No matter if you prefer bold physical confrontation, tactical spellcasting, or the subtle art of stealth, you’ll be able to find gear that supports your choices.

Traverse together with other Nintendo Switch 2 players. You can play with up to two other Tarnished as your cooperative teammates, either by inviting them using a shared password or by summoning them from a pool of nearby community members.

There are also ample opportunities to face off against other players, either through co-op invasions, invited duels, or the many player battle options available in the three Colosseums.

If you’d like to learn more or begin your journey to the Lands Between by pre-ordering the Tarnished Edition, please check out the link below.

He can be found in an IMAX screen, with his eyes watering and his ears bleeding for his own pleasure. He joined the news team in 2022 and accidentally fell upwards into a senior position despite his best efforts. For reasons unknown, he enjoys analyzing box office receipts , giant sharks, and has become known as the go-to man for all things Bosch , Mission: Impossible and Christopher Nolan in Collider's news division. Recently, he found himself yeehawing along to the Dutton saga on the Yellowstone Ranch. He is proficient in sarcasm, wit, Photoshop and working unfeasibly long hours. Amongst his passions sit the likes of the history of the Walt Disney Company, the construction of theme parks , steam trains and binge-watching Gilmore Girls with a coffee that is just hot enough to scald him. His obsession with the Apple TV+ series Silo is the subject of mockery within the Senior News channel, where his feelings about Taylor Sheridan 's work are enough to make his fellow writers roll their eyes. R. Martin’s fantasy fingerprints are still all over some of the biggest stories ever told and, while most fans know him best for Game of Thrones , his work on Elden Ring helped give FromSoftware one of the most detailed and epic fantasy settings in gaming. The Lands Between already made the jump from massive open-world RPG to a film being shot now, but it's expanded through different games and spin-offs and now it's getting another life in a very different format.

A new Elden Ring Nightreign tabletop RPG will officially launch on June 19, 2026, adapting the co-op action RPG of the same name from last year into a pen and paper experience. The game is set in Limveld which is an alternate version of the world as seen in the original Elden Ring, but it's fallen into chaos. Not good. Now it's full of powerful monsters, danger lurking around every corner and hours of suffering. Pretty natural fit for tabletop horror-fantasy fans., even if adapting the speed and intensity of Elden Ring combat into a tabletop format is not exactly the world’s easiest assignment.

For now, the tabletop RPG has only been confirmed for Japan, but an English-language release is not impossible. Other Japanese tabletop games have received English localizations in the past, including adaptations based on major gaming properties like Shin Megami Tensei .

Your answers point to the world your instincts were built for. This is the universe your temperament, your survival instincts, and your particular brand of stubbornness were made for.

You took the red pill a long time ago — probably before anyone offered it to you. You're a systems thinker who can't help but notice the seams in things.

The wasteland doesn't reward the clever or the well-connected — it rewards those who are hard to kill and harder to break. That's you.

You'd survive here because you know how to exist in moral grey areas without losing yourself completely.

Arrakis is the most hostile environment in the known universe — and you are precisely the kind of person it rewards.

The galaxy far, far away is vast, loud, and in a constant state of violent political upheaval — and you wouldn't have it any other way.

Production is underway on the Elden Ring movie, and Alex Garland is writing and directing the live-action adaptation, with the movie set for a March 3, 2028 theatrical release and being filmed for IMAX. The cast is staggering as well, including names as varied as Kit Connor , Cailee Spaeny , Ben Whishaw , Nick Offerman , Tom Burke , Havana Rose Liu , Sonoya Mizuno , Emma Laird , Peter Serafinowicz , Jonathan Pryce , Ruby Cruz , John Hodgkinson , and Jefferson Hall. Martin is onboard as a producer alongside Andrew Macdonald, Allon Reich, Peter Rice, and Vince Gerardis.

The plot of the film is still up in the air a little bit. It's expected to follow the shattered Elden Ring and the corrupted demigods of the Lands Between, but it’s not yet clear whether Garland is adapting the main Tarnished storyline directly or building a new story that he's blending in with the rest.

Elden Ring Nightreign TRPG launches in Japan on June 19, 2026.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE

items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stormveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.
